content:
anya: Quick note — I ran a few nsys captures against the KV-cache regression and hit weird kernel hopping during warmup. Posting captures and flags I used so others can repro.

samir: pls paste the exact nsys command you ran

anya: sure. I tried to keep traces minimal but capture both OSRT and NVTX spans.

anya: command:
```
nsys profile \
  --output=kv_affinity_test \
  --trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt \
  --capture-range=process:$(pidof myserver):start:stop \
  --capture-duration=20s \
  --sample-window=4s \
  --sample-frequency=1000
```
(we use capture-range to avoid huge files; sample-window is our manual short-run to avoid warmup noise)

lee: interesting. where did you set CPU/GPU affinity for the process? warmup often jumps kernels until affinity stabilizes

anya: process is pinned via systemd cpuset to cores 0-7 and CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0

olga: did you try a longer warmup period before starting the trace? the spike at ~200ms looked like JIT/kernel selection settling

anya: yep. I tried 2 warmup modes:
- cold: no warmup (start trace at server start)
- soft-warm: run 10 inference requests (seq len 512) then start trace

samir: can you attach the CLI we used to do the warmup? I want to automate the run in our perf harness

anya: warmup snippet:
```bash
for i in {1..10}; do \
  curl -sS http://localhost:8080/v1/generate -d '{"input":"hello"}' >/dev/null; \
done
# then start nsys capture via harness
```

perf-bot: new capture created: kv_affinity_test.qdrep (size ~120MB) :information_source:

lee: from quick qdrep inspection: early kernels are small fast-gemm variants, then after a few batches runtime switches to a fused-kv kernel with higher latency but better steady throughput. That matches kernel-selection heuristics triggering after cumulative token threshold.

olga: do you see KV cache evictions correlated with that kernel swap? if cache pressure occured we might be choosing a different kernel path

anya: I saw frequent memcpys around the 6s mark — likely KV reshuffle. Sample-window helped pinpoint the hotspot but I want to reproduce with different sample frequencies.

samir: try lowering sample-frequency to avoid losing short-lived kernels. Also experiment with --sample-window around 8s so warmup is fully outside.

anya: will do. plan: run three experiments A/B/C
A) sample-frequency=500, sample-window=4s (current)
B) sample-frequency=2000, sample-window=8s (high freq, longer window)
C) same as B but with a 15s pre-warm (10k tokens)

lee: note: add --trace=osrt so we can see runtime scheduling boundaries; OSRT events expose batch start/finish which helps align kernels to request batches

anya: already included osrt in the trace flag, good call on aligning offsets. Also I added nvtx markers in the server around batching boundaries:
```cpp
NVTX_RANGE_PUSH("batch_start");
// submit batch
NVTX_RANGE_POP();
```

olga: FYI for reproducibility: include --stop-on-exit in harness so capture stops cleanly, otherwise nsight may drop final samples

anya: good tip. I also trimmed capture-range to avoid driver noise from unrelated services. results in a much cleaner kernel timeline.

samir: once you have B and C, can you upload the qdrep and a small notes.txt with which model/config used? I'll run a micro-analysis script to see if kernel selection threshold is tied to tokens-per-batch

anya: will upload to //artifacts/perf/kv-affinity/ with naming: kv_affinity_{mode}_{freq}.qdrep and kv_affinity_{mode}_{freq}.notes

lee: if kernel swapping is purely heuristics, short-term mitigation: pin the model to a particular kernel via env override (dev-only) or force quantization path. Useful as temporary bandage for production until we fix selection logic.

anya: documenting temporary env flag: MODEL_KERNEL_HINT=fused_kv_fast

olga: add regression check to CI: run 1s nsys sampling with same flags on PRs that touch kernel-selection or batching heuristics. If kernel transitions happen in the first N batches, fail the PR.

perf-bot: action item created: PERF-2432 "Investigate kernel-selection oscillation on KV-heavy loads" assigned to samir/anya, due 2026-04-10

anya: thanks. I'll post follow-up with B/C captures and a short TL;DR about whether it's warmup, KV-evict pressure, or heuristic nudging. :thumbsup:
